definitions.explanation: Refers to expressions, phrases, or usages that have become established through long custom and repeated use, even if they may not follow strict grammatical or semantic rules.

examples.japanese: {慣用|かんよう}{句|く}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{覚|おぼ}える→覚える：00739_oboeru⟧。
⟦これ→これ：00963_kore⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{慣用|かんよう}⟦{的|てき}→〜的：09839_teki⟧な⟦{言|い}い{方|かた}→言い方：14165_iikata⟧だ。
examples.english: This is an idiomatic way of saying it.

examples.japanese: 「⟦{的|まと}→的：19356_mato⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{射|い}る」⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{正|ただ}しい→正しい：00893_tadashii⟧{慣用|かんよう}⟦{表現|ひょうげん}→表現：03584_hyougen⟧だ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、「⟦{的|まと}→的：19356_mato⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{得|え}る→得る：02014_eru⟧」⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{広|ひろ}く→広い：00704_hiroi⟧⟦{使|つか}われている→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
examples.english: "Mato o iru" is the correct idiomatic expression, but "mato o eru" is also widely used.

notes:
USAGE:
Most commonly seen in the compound {慣用|かんよう}{句|く} (idiomatic phrase/idiom). Also used as a no-adjective ({慣用|かんよう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧) or with ～⟦{的|てき}→〜的：09839_teki⟧ ({慣用|かんよう}⟦{的|てき}→〜的：09839_teki⟧). In linguistics, {慣用|かんよう}⟦{読|よ}み→読み：00425_yomi⟧ refers to a customary reading of kanji that differs from the standard reading.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {慣用|かんよう}{句|く}: idiomatic expression, idiom
- {慣用|かんよう}⟦{表現|ひょうげん}→表現：03584_hyougen⟧: idiomatic expression
- {慣用|かんよう}⟦{読|よ}み→読み：00425_yomi⟧: customary reading (of kanji)
- {慣用|かんよう}⟦{的|てき}→〜的：09839_teki⟧: idiomatic, conventional
